name: Bokor
body:
Archetypes

Houngan (Bokor Archetype)

A bokor practices the forbidden art of black magic. They ritually create a soul ward, fueled by their own life force energy, that both protects them and allows them to tap into the collective powers of all the gods (“Bon Dieu” in their nomenclature). They serve no deity and clerics oft regard them as heretics. Bokor use their powerful black magic to manipulate life and death. Though feared by many they are not without virtue, turning the darkness against the wicked. Armed with potent black magics, loyal undead and the will to do whatever they need to get ahead, bokor are truly a force to be reckoned with.

Many bokor are shaman-like figures that lead backwater settlements and tribes. Goblinoid creatures are particularly given to having bokor as spiritual leaders. While bokor often exist on the fringes of societies like druids or witches, their ambition often leads to them finding themselves into positions of power and society. They have served as mystic advisors to kings, undead commanders to wicked liches, and or warlords in their own right.

Hit Die: d6

Alignment: Any

Starting Wealth: 2d6 × 10 gp (average 70 gp.) In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The bokor’s class skills are Appraise (Int), Craft (Int), Fly (Dex), Knowledge (all) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Profession (Wis), and Spellcraft (Int).

Skill Ranks per Level: 2 + Int modifier.

Class Features

The following are the class features of the Bokor.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Bokor are proficient with the club, dagger, heavy crossbow, light crossbow, and quarterstaff, but not with any type of armor or shield. Armor interferes with a bokor’s movements, which can cause his spells with somatic components to fail.

Soul Ward (Su)

An intangible field of siphoned soul energy protects a bokor from destruction. This ward has a maximum number of hit points as indicated on Table: The Bokor, but starts at half this amount each day. A bokor’s soul ward only lasts 24 hours due to a connection the ward has with the solar/lunar cycles (a soul ward cannot be formed during an eclipse).

Each day a bokor must take 1 hour to reform his soul ward. A soul ward may only be restored health by the soul drain and consume soul class features (not by normal or magical healing for example).

Whenever a bokor would be reduced below 1 hit point, all damage in excess of that which would reduce it to 1 hit point is instead dealt to its soul ward. If this damage reduces the soul ward to fewer than 0 hit points, the bokor can be reduced below zero hit points. If a soul ward is broken, it takes 1 hour to restore the ward. A soul ward functions in a similar way to the special ability of a creature with the ravener template.

Sidebar

Unholy damage is damage resulting from unholy power and is, like in the balor’s entry, not subject to damage reduction (only by resistance to unholy damage). This damage is not negative energy damage and does not heal undead.

Spell Casting

A bokor casts arcane spells drawn primarily from the sorcerer/wizard spell list. Unlike other spellcasters, a bokor does not have spell slots. Instead, whenever the bokor wishes to cast any one of his spells known, he consumes a number of hit points from his soul ward equal to the spell slot level necessary to cast the spell (including increased levels for metamagic feats and so on). If the soul ward has insufficient hit points, the bokor cannot cast that spell. Casting a spell that reduces its soul ward to exactly 0 hit points does not harm the bokor (though most are not comfortable without this buffer of soul-energy and try to replenish it quickly).

To learn, prepare, or cast a spell, the bokor must have an Intelligence score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a bokor’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the bokor’s Intelligence modifier.

A bokor’s selection of spells is extremely limited. A bokor begins play knowing four 1st-level spells of his choice. At each new bokor level, he gains one or more new spells, as indicated on Table: Bokor Spells Known. (The number of spells a bokor knows is not affected by his Intelligence score; the numbers on Table: Bokor Spells Known are fixed.) These new spells can be common spells chosen from the sorcerer/wizard spell list, or they can be unusual spells that the bokor has gained some understanding of through study.

Upon reaching 4th level, and at every even-numbered bokor level after that (6th, 8th, and so on), a bokor can choose to learn a new spell in place of one he already knows. In effect, the bokor loses the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged. A bokor may swap only a single spell at any given even level, and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that he gains new spells known for the level. Unlike a wizard or a cleric, a bokor need not prepare his spells in advance. He can cast any spell he knows at any time, assuming he has remaining hit points in his soul ward.

Soul Drain (Su)

The bokor may make an attack with his soul drain blast as a standard action. A soul drain is a blast of unholy energy that functions as a ranged touch attack that drains health from its target. The bokor’s soul drain deals 1d4 unholy damage at 1st level and an additional 1d4 damage every 2 levels thereafter. A soul drain has a range increment of 60 feet and a x2 critical modifier. A bokor can only make one such attack per round. A creature hit by a soul drain must pass a Fortitude (DC = 10 + 1/2 bokor level + Intelligence Modifier) save or take 1 negative level. If a creature takes a negative level from soul drain, this adds a number of hit points to the bokor’s soul ward equal to the creature’s Hit Dice.

Animate Dead (Sp)

At 2nd level a bokor use his stolen soul energy to animate corpses. He can pay an amount of Hit Points from his soul ward equal to a dead creature’s HD to reanimate it as if by animate dead as a spell-like ability. At 10th level he can use create undead in the same fashion and at 14th level it improves to create greater undead.

Consume Soul (Su)

At 4th level, when a living creature within 30 feet of a bokor drops below zero HP, that creature’s soul can be taken and captured. As an immediate action to a creature being dropped below zero hit points, a bokor can consume the soul of a dying creature if it fails a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 bokor level + Intelligence modifier). This adds a number of hit points to the bokor’s soul ward equal to the dead creature’s Hit Dice. Creatures that have their souls consumed in this way can only be brought back to life through miracle, true resurrection, or wish.

Undead Commander (Ex)

At 8th level a bokor’s caster level is considered to be 3 higher for the purposes of determining what kind of undead he can create with his animate dead, create undead, and create greater undead spells.

Grand Bokor (Ex)

At 20th level a bokor can chose to perform a ritual (costing 1,000gp) to transform themselves into a juju zombie with the following notes. Their alignment doesn’t need to be evil, they are perfectly intelligent and even retains a degree of grace and poise. A bokor can choose not to becomes a juju zombie or may delay doing the ritual as long as he wishes.

Playing a Bokor

Playing a bokor is like playing a resource management game. You need to ration your spells because casting them consumes your soul ward. While you can restore your soul ward with your soul drain class feature you need to be careful that you don’t outpace your rate of consumption of soul ward HP from other creatures. Inflicting a negative level on a creature is a nasty penalty and restores your soul ward’s HP. At 4th level you can rely on consume soul to restore soul ward’s HP. This is a powerful mechanic you need to learn to manipulate in order to excel as a bokor, particularly at low level. At level 1-3 you have between 1-6 HP in your soul ward and this makes you vulnerable to running out of spells very quickly. Around mid to late game you won’t have to worry about running out of HP in the ward as you should have enough to sustain yourself.

A bokor’s soul ward’s benefit is twofold. It provides you access to spellcasting but can also prevent an untimely demise. At 20th level it provides a whopping extra 270 HP! If a bokor has a good Constitution score they can be a meaty caster despite the d6 hit dice it has. Intelligence, the primary casting stat of a bokor, is also very important to maintain.
